key_insight: HippoCamp introduces a realistic benchmark that evaluates agents on multimodal, device-scale personal file systems—testing their ability to model user profiles and search massive personal files for context-aware reasoning.
problem_solved: Existing agent benchmarks target web interaction, tool use, or generic automation and do not measure how well agents understand and act within personalized, multimodal file environments on personal devices.
method: Construct device-scale, realistic file-system environments mapped to diverse real-world user profiles and modalities (text, images, audio, video, email, etc.).
Design tasks that require agents to infer user intent/profile, retrieve relevant context from large local corpora, and produce context-aware responses or actions.
Measure agent performance with metrics emphasizing relevance, contextual understanding, retrieval efficiency, and robustness across users and modalities.
impact: HippoCamp enables more realistic evaluation of personal-AI capabilities, guiding development of agents that safely and effectively manage users' multimodal personal data and make contextually appropriate decisions.
visual_elements: Schematic of a device-scale file system with layered modalities (icons for text, images, audio, video, email) feeding into an agent
Pipeline diagram: User profile → Contextual search/retrieval → Reasoning/response → Action/summary
Bar/heatmap comparison of agent performance across metrics (relevance, recall, latency) and user profiles
Example case study card showing a multimodal query and the agent's retrieved context and final answer
paper_title: HippoCamp: Benchmarking Contextual Agents on Personal Computers
paper_authors: Zhe Yang, Shulin Tian, Kairui Hu, Shuai Liu, Hoang-Nhat Nguyen
